fixes.explanation: That's right. God says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does say He will send an angel before them, but He Himself won't be going along. I think that line landed hard on everyone who heard it.

I see why you'd pick it, but test isn't the word in this verse. God says “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). That's a much heavier word than test. He says it again two verses later: “If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.” (Exodus 33:5).

Yes, friend. The verse says “…no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The people had just heard the bad news, and they went into mourning. Then verse 6 says the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

Sandals never come up, friend. The verse says the people “…went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The only thing it names is jewelry. I'll keep my sandals out of this one anyway, since I'm a stamper standing on a gold base.

Armor is a bold guess, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The people heard bad news, and the text says they “…went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The word that fits the blank is jewelry.

That's right. “As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). The cloud comes down, and then the LORD speaks. Verse 7 says anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to this tent outside the camp.

Writing laws isn't what happens in this scene, friend. The verse says, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). What happens next is the LORD speaking. Nothing about writing shows up in these verses.

Yes, friend. “When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). They didn't have to walk to the tent. Verse 8 says they would stand at their own tent entrances and watch Moses until he went in, so they were already right there.

Yes, baker! “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is the heart of the scene. And right after it, Moses speaks to the LORD and the LORD answers him (Exodus 33:12–14).

That's him! “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Moses heads back to camp, but Joshua stays put in the tent. The text doesn't say why he stayed, and I'd love to know.

That's right. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). Moses is asking to know the LORD better, and that's a good thing to ask for. Then he adds, “Remember that this nation is Your people.” (Exodus 33:13). He asks for himself, and then he speaks up for the people.

Yes! The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Back in verse 3 He had said He would not go with them. Here He speaks of His own Presence going, and of rest. After all that bad news, rest is a nice word to hear.
That's not what He says. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). It's His Presence that goes. Nothing in that answer sends Moses off on his own.

That's right. Moses asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). To Moses, God going with them is how it can be known. He then asks a second question in the very same verse about being distinguished from all the other people.

Yes, friend. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). In his words, God going with them is what sets them apart. Moses packs two questions into one verse. That's efficient talking.

Yes, baker. Moses says, “Please show me Your glory.” (Exodus 33:18). The LORD had just said yes to his last request in verse 17, and Moses asks for more. I'd have been nervous asking again, but Moses just asks it plainly.

That's it. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). Moses asked to see His glory, and the LORD answers that He will cause all His goodness to pass before Moses. Right there in the same verse He adds, “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.” (Exodus 33:19).

A new set of laws would make a big announcement, but that's not what this verse says. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). What gets proclaimed is His name, said right there with Moses. No rulebook this time, just the name.

That's right. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives, and it's a serious one. He doesn't say no and leave it there, though. In the next verses He tells Moses where to stand on a rock and what He will do (Exodus 33:21–23).

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Moses gets to see His back, and the face must not be seen. Before that, the LORD says He will put Moses in a cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand until He has passed by (Exodus 33:22).

Feet is a fun guess, and I love a fun guess, but the LORD doesn't use that word. He says, “…you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Verse 22 has His hand covering Moses until He has passed by, and then the hand comes away. The word that goes in the blank is back.
